code:
import os
import sys

DEBUG = os.environ.get("DEBUG", "0") == "1"

def eval_expr(expr, env):
    if DEBUG:
        print(f"[eval] {expr}", file=sys.stderr)
    # ... rest of evaluator ...
description: A DEBUG flag read from the environment that turns on debug output to stderr, without changing any command-line argument parsing.

steps.description: The page says environment variables let you add debug flags without changing any source file or command-line parsing. This imports `os` and `sys`, then sets `DEBUG` from the environment.
`os.environ.get("DEBUG", "0")` returns the value of `DEBUG` when it is set, or `"0"` when it is not. Comparing the result to `"1"` gives a boolean.
`eval_expr` checks `DEBUG` and prints the expression to `sys.stderr`. The page says writing debug output to stderr keeps it separate from program output, so your diff-based tests still work.
